detail: Mubit trained an enterprise Qwen3 4B adapter after accepting 28 examples. It passed 11 of 12 internal checks. Fresh testing found important gaps, so live assessments continue to use Luna.

baseline.scope: DEVELOPMENT diagnostic; no trained adapter comparison

review_provenance.reviewer: coding assistant, not an independent enterprise expert
review_provenance.authorization: User explicitly authorized testing the idea fully with judgement.

evaluation.scope: Six frozen DEVELOPMENT questions; one attempt each, no correction note, target, retry or repair.
evaluation.summary: 2 of 6 met the substantive judgement rubric, with 1 uncertain and 3 failing. Only 1 of 6 matched the app response format; none passed both checks. This is a small diagnostic, not a controlled before-and-after result.
evaluation.schema_diagnostic: A separate new HSBC prompt included the response schema explicitly and produced a valid format. It is excluded from the original six scores; preview schema/settings differences limit interpretation.
evaluation.limitations: The preview does not expose the full system prompt, response schema or generation settings. There is no matched untrained base control on these six questions. Reviews are by the coding assistant. No cost or speed advantage is established.

cases.question: Morgan Stanley already has an AI assistant. Why would we still pitch Mubit, and what exactly should we trial?
cases.reason: Grounded complementary pilot, advisor reviewer, ownership/hosting optionality and held-out examples. It does not explicitly freeze fresh questions; conservative rubric leaves this uncertain.
